Senses.Explanation: My hand — how does it resemble the buddha's hand? The pass belongs to Huanglong Huinan's room: he would ask a monk where his birth-place is, and mid-exchange thrust out his hand — my hand, how does it resemble the buddha's hand? — then dangle his foot; thirty-odd years he showed these three questions, scholars rarely matched his intent, and the school named them the three barriers. Zhenjing Kewen ran it on the young Zhantang Wenzhun: where from — Great Yang; where spent the summer — Great Wei; what place's man — Xingyuan-fu; and then the hands spread — my hand, how does it resemble the buddha's hand? — and Zhantang stands at a loss; Zhenjing diagnoses him: your answers just now were each one numinous and innate, and the moment buddha-hand was said it became stoppage — where is the sickness? I don't understand. Everything is ready-made — whom else should it teach? Huanxi Weiyi answers all three in the evening assembly: my hand — how does it resemble the buddha's hand? ten fingers uneven; my foot — how does it resemble a donkey's foot? four hooves treading the ground; everyone has a birth-place — ears, two sheets of skin; teeth, one set of bone; so understanding it, one sees the Jicui old man's face right here, sharing every drink and every enjoyment with you, betraying no one, favoring no one. Zhongfeng Mingben versifies the triad: the hand too can pluck flowers and snap willows; the scale-weight drops by the bed, the smoothing-iron breaks before the stove; the foot turns the straw sandal and walks it backwards across the four great continents without one step ever treading; and the birth-place — a macaque at the tiller at midnight, smashing through black wind and white waves to tread the sky beneath the water; buddha-hand, donkey-foot, birth-place — one phrase declares all three; ask what then? Huanglong's mouth holds no drool. And Sanyi Mingyu turns the pass on the imitators: those who climb into the curio-bag and learn resemblance-words — asked the hand-question, they answer plucking the pipa beneath the moon; asked the foot, standing in boots on the water; asked their birth-place, I am a man of Xiu Prefecture — leaning on walls, weak wings on low branches, words never once leaving the ruts: how could they climb out of the covering tangles, sunk as they are in the aggregate-demon realm. Yingning Zhijing sets the test in the ancestors' kindness: every device, every setting, every phrase must split open your face-gate and dry up your consciousness-waves — thus Huanglong tested people with three lines; few in his life matched his trigger, the school named them the three barriers, and through old and new many have capped them, many misread them; borne by that grace he versifies all three — the map runs out and suddenly the dagger shows; First Emperor sees it and his soul flies. Feiyin Tongrong runs the passes live on Lingyue: talking together, he suddenly thrusts out his hand — my hand, how does it resemble the buddha's hand? Lingyue: stop showing off. The foot comes out — worse and worse. Everyone has a birth-place; where is yours? Face to face, not recognized. Apart from the three passes, what then? Lingyue shouts; a good thirty blows; and Lingyue's comeback — the master himself is not without fault — ends it. Yinyuan Longqi, after laying out the room-story in prose, answers in his own verse: my hand — how does it resemble the buddha's hand? this — who lacks it? flip the original face over, and laugh that he still does not know shame; my foot — how does it resemble a donkey's foot? why stretch and bend it before others; not yet past the Huanglong barrier — no wonder it still obstructs you. And Yun'e Xi drags a donkey up into the hall: a ready-made case — one turning word that matches, and the staff and the whisk are handed over; the foot lifts — my foot, how does it resemble a donkey's foot? — the hand rises — my hand, how does it resemble the buddha's hand? — everyone has a birth-place, where is yours? The assembly's answers all miss, so he takes their place at every station — just bow — and versifies it: the hand stretching, folding, lifting, laying hold of what was always there.
